newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AMBROSE MAKES IMMEDIATE IMPACT ON RETURN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE MAKES IMMEDIATE IMPACT ON RETURN.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Curtly Ambrose made an immediate impact on his return from injury to lift his side's spirits in the opening session of the fifth and final test against Australia on Saturday.
Ambrose dismissed opener Matthew Hayden for a duck with the third ball of the match and Steve Waugh for one as the West Indies tore through Australia's top order.
At lunch at the WACA Ground, Australia were 59 for four in their first innings after captain Mark Taylor won the toss and elected to bat.
It was a remarkable transformation for the tourists as they sought to restore their pride after Australia retained the Frank Worrell trophy by taking an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series.
Ambrose missed West Indies' crushing innings defeat in the fourth test in Adelaide and immediately underlined his importance to the team with figures of two for 13 from 10 overs in the session.
Hayden fended at a ball pitching outside the line of his off-stump only to edge a simple, waist-high catch to Brian Lara at first slip.
The first wicket went down without a run on the board and Australia soon found themselves in even deeper trouble when Taylor was run out for two with the total on seven.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul, fielding at cover point, produced a brilliant stop and quick, accurate throw to run out Taylor by a matter of inches at the striker's end.
Number three Greg Blewett survived for 82 minutes before losing his wicket to the medium pace of all-rounder Phil Simmons for 17.
After struggling badly in Ambrose's second spell of the session, Steve Waugh attempted to cut a wide delivery but only succeeded in edging the ball to Courtney Browne.
Mark Waugh was unbeaten on 26 alongside Michael Bevan on four not out at the break.
